summary: Unexpected dedicated pool slowdown correlated with infrequent client heartbeats
description: Issue summary: QuickReply AI reported a drop in sustained throughput and spike in p99 latency for routes pinned to their dedicated capacity pool starting 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC. Impact: customer-facing inference latency p50 doubled from ~40ms to ~80ms and p99 increased from ~300ms to ~1.6s across multiple models. Business impact: degraded SLA for dedicated tenant, customer-visible latency spikes during normal traffic patterns. Environment: dedicated reserved pool (tenant id qreply-07), prod-us-east, mixed short/long streams. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of short-chat requests (avg tokens 32) to tenant-pinned route for 30+ minutes. 2) Observe prewarm events and periodic GPU attach/detach cycles. 3) Notice p99 spikes align with quiet periods of incoming traffic (10-15 minute gaps). Observed metrics & artifacts: - Autoscaler logs show repeated deallocations/reallocations during periods where prefix heartbeats are sparse. - slot_allocation.rebalance_count increased by ~3x compared to baseline. - NVLink and PCIe IO counters show short bursts coincident with allocation events. - Serving runtime traces show frequent KV cache invalidations followed by cold-cache token generation latency. - Customer evidence indicates the client sends keepalive/heartbeat at irregular long intervals (typical client heartbeat TTL ~12 minutes from customer side) rather than steady micro-heartbeats. Preliminary hypothesis: infrequent client heartbeats lead to allocator marking streams as idle, triggering slot rebalancing and prewarm/attach workflows. When a new request arrives after the quiet period, runtime must reattach or reinitialize kernels and KV cache, causing short bursts of GPU driver/IO activity and increased tail latency. This pattern looks like a "latency pendulum" where the system oscillates between warm and cold states driven by noisy heartbeat/lease signals rather than sustained inference demand.
comments: Support (2026-03-10): Acknowledged ticket and requested request IDs, sample request timestamps and route names. Assigned to Miguel for SRE investigation.
Customer (QuickReply AI) (2026-03-10): Provided sample request IDs and client-side keepalive config. Notes that clients use long-polling users that often idle for 8-15 minutes between messages.

SRE (Miguel) (2026-03-11): Observed correlation between heartbeat gaps and autoscaler dealloc events. Captured allocation timeline and attached aggregated metrics (link in confluence). Noticed KV cache invalidations at dealloc boundary.

SRE (2026-03-12): Performed controlled test by adjusting QuickReply heartbeat to 30s using a test API key; p99 dropped back to baseline and prewarm events largely disappeared. Requested customer to trial reduced heartbeat interval as workaround.
Customer (2026-03-12): Applied temporary client-side change to send 30s micro-heartbeats for a pilot subset. Reported immediate improvement in P50/P99 and asked for recommended long-term fix.

Support (2026-03-13): Noted potential platform mitigations: tenant-affinity grace window increase, slower deallocation backoff for dedicated pools with mixed short streams, and prewarm triggers based on recent tail-call frequency rather than strict heartbeat TTL alone. Escalated to Platform Eng for design.
Platform Eng (2026-03-13): Requested telemetry samples and suggested a patch to extend idle-grace to 20m for dedicated pools as a stopgap. Opened PR for autoscaler backoff tuning (see linked PR).
investigation_notes: 1) Timeline reconstruction: repeated pattern of 'quiet period (~10-15m) -> client message -> autoscaler observed burst -> dealloc/realloc -> p99 spike'.

2) Autoscaler behavior: current conservative idle detection uses heartbeat TTL and stream activity counters; quiet intervals allowed allocator to compact slots aggressively in this pool due to slot fragmentation heuristics.
3) Serving runtime: cold KV cache miss cost ~0.9s at p99 when kernel reinitialization and PCIe/KV shuffle occurs; NVLink counters show short-lived saturation during these events.
4) No evidence of GPU driver crashes or hardware faults. Resource metrics show transient IO contention and elevated GPU attach latency.
5) QuickReply's client pattern (sparse human-chat interactions) is common for chat apps and not well-served by current short idle timeouts in dedicated pools.
6) Repro test: toggling heartbeat frequency to 30s eliminated most dealloc cycles and reduced p99 by ~65% in test window.

7) Risk assessment: increasing idle-grace will increase reserved slot utilization and could modestly reduce overall pool packing efficiency; however impact is acceptable for enterprise/dedicated tenants with SLA guarantees.

8) Related prior tickets: SUP-33489 (small-stream fanout causing slot churn) and SUP-421900 (prefetch locks causing throughput plateau) show similar patterns but differ in root cause; this one is driven by client-side heartbeat cadence.
resolution_notes: Workaround implemented: Customer applied 30s micro-heartbeat in clients for pilot subset; immediate improvement confirmed (p99 reduced to ~320ms during pilot).

Short-term platform mitigation: Increased idle-grace window for tenant qreply-07 from 5m to 20m (config change deployed to autoscaler in prod-us-east). Monitoring is in place for packing efficiency and slot utilization.

Medium-term plan: Platform Eng to implement autoscaler heuristic that weighs recent request frequency and average inter-request interval before compaction decisions for dedicated pools. Target RFC and implementation timeline: RFC by 2026-03-21, rollout by 2026-04-04.

Follow-up actions: 1) Notify QuickReply of permanent recommended client heartbeat guidance; 2) Add a dedicated tenant autoscaler profile option exposed in Console ("chatty human idle profile") for customers with sparse human interactions; 3) Add automated alert if slot_compaction_rate spikes >2x baseline for a tenant.
Status: Partial mitigation applied; ticket will remain open until autoscaler heuristic change is implemented and monitored for 7 days post-rollout.
Post-mortem link (pending): will link to Confluence after RFC and rollout closure.
